resources.string: Format JSON, XML attributes or CSS rule boundaries, or normalize HTML locally.

Choose JSON, XML, HTML or CSS. JSON supports validation, pretty-printing and minification; XML supports validation or conservative attribute layout; HTML supports full-document normalization only; CSS supports conservative top-level rule separation. Explicitly run the operation. Processing stays local; automatic history and result saving are off by default.
Try a small object with a name string and an enabled boolean, then explicitly format or validate it.

JSON, XML 1.0, HTML normalization and conservative CSS rule separation. CSS layout is not validation, sanitization, minification or full beautification. HTML repairs and wraps fragments, may change markup, and is not validation or sanitization. XML rejects DTDs and external entities; formatting preserves content and changes only attribute layout, not tree indentation. Duplicate object keys are rejected rather than silently overwritten. Input and nesting limits apply. Valid syntax does not prove data is safe or matches a schema; review before copying or sharing private content.
Load a small object with a name string and an enabled boolean, then explicitly run pretty-printing.
